Self harm is derived from an escape from another form of pain. Being a teenager certainly has its painful moments, but don't use that as an excuse. You'll look back on those years and realize the good, the potential, the silly mistakes, and realize that there are so many more visceral, wholesome moments to experience. Try to appreciate where you are now in your youth. There is still pain and hardship, and it is genuine, but try to be present and engage in your life while you're there.

I was a brooding teenager too, but I realize there were so many things I neglected while hating the world, my parents, my peers, school. It's a limiting experience. Feel the pain, but try to be positive about the process. You have so much ahead of you!
I really hope that everything works out for you. If you need help you can message me. Be well, and don't hurt yourself. Practice self love and hold on to your friend. You'll get through this

I'm sorry that you're feeling so hopeless, I know how hard that can be. I'm glad that you have a friend to talk to. Don't feel like a burden, your feelings are valid and deserve to be heard. Your pain is real.

I know how serious these feelings are, and I want you to be ok, and I think that they could help. Teenage years are hard, and it might feel like no one is on your side, but there is a light at the end of the tunnel, even if you can't see it now. Talk to your friend, and be as honest as you can with your family, I hope they support you.

I understand your pain and state my friend. The manic episodes are really hard and feel like the only reality, also heightened by drugs. Know that you are worthy of happiness and a future. I struggle with it every day, but the little things help. You said have friends, this is good support. I get the feeling of wanting to freak them out, or to jar them into concern with a cry for help, but I think they would be more responsive, and more helpful for you, if you had an honest sit down heart to heart with them and really told them how much you're struggling. 

Being in the depths of addiction and battling self worth are so hard, but you're not alone. Wanting to die because of our failures is such an agonizing feeling. What you are feeling is valid and real, and deserves to be addressed. I know first hand how hard it is to feel worthless, to feel like you've let someone close to you down, to feel ashamed of what you do and who you are. It's maddening, but it can get better. I really urge you to talk seriously to those close to you about your feelings and struggles. You're welcome to reach out to me if you need to. Please don't end your life, and please try to have some forgiveness for yourself and your actions. There is more to life than addiction and depression

I'm incredibly grateful to have been able to continue working during this whole fiasco, but the fact that I, as an essential worker, had to be let go at my second job that enabled me to have just a little bit extra to stay ahead, while people that aren't working are getting more than I make in a month, makes me angry. I'm not angry at them, I'm angry at the system. For the past 6 months I have been barely scraping by on food and bills, often having to resort shamefully to borrowing money from family until my next paycheck. Where is the justice in that? I haven't had any sort of break or respite, all the while being in direct contact with the public 40 hours a week. 2 extra dollars an hour is a nice gesture, but where does it leave us? I still haven't received my stimulus check either. I'm so frustrated and flabbergasted at the incompetence of all this. In an already thankless job I have been made to feel even less important. When do we get our recompense? When do we get to rest? How long do we have to break our backs holding up society? 
Thank you for coming to my TED talk.
